docs.title: Listing journey and item
docs.summary: Seller input, validation, Listing creation, QC and downstream content distribution.

sections.heading: The journey shown in the slide
sections.body: Product information enters through seller-facing inputs, passes upload validation, is stored as a Listing item, and goes through Listing quality checks. Passing QC leads to content distribution to buyer surfaces; QC failure leads to treatment. The slide also shows later content optimisation.

sections.heading: How to use this
sections.body: When investigating an item, locate the seller input, validation result, current status, QC outcome and affected buyer surface.

docs.title: Item status and buyer visibility
docs.summary: Normal status appears in search; other statuses have different buyer-surface visibility.

sections.heading: Status and visibility are different questions
sections.body: The workbook note says item status mainly reflects the item's position in QC. The checked table marks Normal visible in search, recommendations, shop and PDP. Reviewing, banned, deleted and blacklisted entries are not shown in those surfaces in this table.

sections.heading: A useful investigation question
sections.body: Ask for the exact item status and affected surface. Do not assume a seller-visible item is searchable by buyers.

docs.title: Category and product data
docs.summary: BE category, buyer-facing FE category, attributes and listing fields.

sections.heading: Category roles
sections.body: The workbook distinguishes BE/Global Category, used as a seller-side convention across regions, from FE/Local/Display Category, used by buyers and promotions. It notes that attributes can narrow a category and may be mandatory or optional.

sections.heading: Product fields
sections.body: The item notes list images, variations and price among data to inspect. Category selection reaches an end leaf node in the workbook example; actual depth depends on the category tree.

docs.title: Merchant, marketplace SKU and merchant SKU
docs.summary: Merchant, shop, MP and MT SKU relationships, plus the basic VSKU idea.

sections.heading: Entity links in the notes
sections.body: Cell AC52 says one merchant can have many shops and MT SKUs. Cell AF52 describes MT SKU as a physical item and says one MT SKU can map to many MP SKUs. Q53 describes a shop as an online store that does not cross markets and MP SKU as the marketplace listing management unit.

sections.heading: Before debugging
sections.body: Identify which shop, MP listing and MT item the question refers to. Read the original VSKU and supplier notes before applying those rules to a real case.

sections.heading: VSKU at a glance
sections.body: Cell R96 describes a VSKU as a virtual item combining multiple real SKUs into a package. Treat the detailed composition and fulfilment limits as source-specific material to confirm with the current owner.

docs.title: Stock basics: sellable, reserved and locked
docs.summary: A basic stock vocabulary and available quantity relationship.

sections.heading: Three quantities
sections.body: The checked slide describes sellable as physical stock, reserved as stock held for promotions or virtual SKUs, and locked as stock held around order placement or sourcing. It distinguishes warehouse and seller location behaviour.

sections.heading: Available
sections.body: The workbook expresses available stock as sellable minus reserved minus locked, where locked applies. Treat this as a learning model; use current system definitions for operational calculations.

docs.title: Advanced stock concepts
docs.summary: Reserved modes, shared stock, VSKU and partial fulfilment require separate review.

sections.heading: Where to look next
sections.body: The workbook contains separate notes on fixed and floating reservation modes, MT/MP sharing, virtual SKU composition and partial fulfilment. These are complex and contain draft or conflict signals. Open the original cell and slide before using any rule for a decision.

docs.title: What Keypee can do
docs.summary: Learn by day, search workbook sources, draft a task plan and ask DeepSeek.

sections.heading: In this prototype
sections.body: Keypee has a five-day learning path, a searchable workbook-based Knowledge Hub, a local notes collection, an AI chat, and three demo task workflows. EOD and manager review forms are local drafts only. No company systems or calendar are connected.

launch.label: Feature launch
steps: Read the brief, align success criteria and identify open decisions.
Confirm stakeholders, technical dependencies and proposed timeline.
Draft cases and confirm test environment and access.
Execute cases, log reproducible issues and retest.
Bring the action plan and evidence to the manager checkpoint.
Confirm rollout steps and watch agreed signals.

investigation.label: Issue investigation
steps: Capture scope, expected versus actual behaviour and reproduction.
Trace relevant flow and data with the owner.
Retest and update stakeholders with evidence.

analysis.label: Data analysis
steps: Define the business question, metric, grain, filters and time window.
Confirm sources, permissions and data quality.
Discuss implications and next action with owners.
